title: Kenyan Sweet Potato Pudding
community: Popular across Kenya — a comforting traditional dessert
author: Mama Wanjiru
desc: Kenyan Sweet Potato Pudding — mashed orange sweet potato blended with coconut milk, eggs, brown sugar, cinnamon, and nutmeg, then baked until set into a soft, fragrant, naturally sweet pudding. A beautifully simple Kenyan dessert that lets the sweet potato shine.
longDesc: Sweet potato pudding is one of the most satisfying ways to finish a Kenyan meal — the natural sweetness and vibrant orange colour of Kenyan sweet potatoes need very little enhancement. Coconut milk adds richness, warm spices add depth, and the baked result is a pudding that is simultaneously homely and special. It appears at family celebrations and everyday tables alike.
ingredients: 600g orange-fleshed sweet potatoes — peeled, boiled, and mashed
steps: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease a baking dish.
Mash the boiled sweet potatoes until completely smooth — no lumps.
Whisk coconut milk, eggs, brown sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger, vanilla, salt, and melted butter together.
Combine with the mashed sweet potato. Mix until smooth.
Pour into the greased baking dish.
Bake for 35—40 minutes until the top is set and lightly golden.
Allow to cool for 10 minutes before serving.
Serve warm or at room temperature.
chefTips: The smoother the mashed sweet potato, the silkier the pudding — use a food processor for the smoothest result.
Brown sugar adds a caramel depth that white sugar does not.
Do not overbake — the pudding should be set but still have a slight jiggle in the centre.
commonMistakes: Lumpy sweet potato — creates a textured rather than smooth pudding.

faqs.q: Can I make this without eggs?
faqs.a: Yes — replace eggs with 2 tbsp of cornstarch dissolved in 4 tbsp water. The pudding will be slightly less firm but still delicious.

cookingScience: Eggs in the pudding provide structure through protein coagulation during baking. The high beta-carotene content of orange sweet potatoes is fat-soluble — the coconut milk in the recipe actually enhances its absorption, making this dessert more nutritious than it appears.
sustainabilityTips: Sweet potatoes are one of the most sustainable crops — drought-resistant and nutritious.
reheating: Warm in oven at 160°C for 10 minutes or microwave briefly.
healthBenefits: Good source of vitamins A and C.
Natural sweetness reduces need for added sugar.
culturalNote: Sweet potato pudding represents the Kenyan kitchen's instinct to find sweetness and comfort in the everyday ingredients of the homestead garden — transforming a simple root vegetable into something celebratory.
